explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - NetAlertX is a full-stack, containerized network-scanning and alert system. It provides:  
     • A web UI (PHP + JavaScript) served by Nginx + PHP-FPM  
     • A Python-based API layer (REST, GraphQL)  
     • A scheduler/worker subsystem for scans and workflows  
     • A plugin framework for scanners and notification gateways  
     • A SQLite data store for configuration and events  

2. Top-level structure & architectural patterns  
   - Directories of note:  
     • front/ → PHP code, UI templates, JS/CSS assets, plugin scripts  
     • server/ → Python API server, DB abstractions, scheduler, workflows, messaging  
     • back/ + cron_script.sh → legacy cron wrapper  
     • config/, db/ → runtime volumes (host-mounted in Docker)  
     • Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml → multi-service container orchestration  
   - Pattern: Monolithic container running multiple “services”  
     (Nginx, PHP-FPM, Cron, Python server)  
   - Plugin-based modularity: script files in front/plugins and server/plugin_utils  

3. Core components & interactions  
   a. Web UI layer  
     • Nginx proxy / static assets → routes PHP requests to PHP-FPM  
     • PHP-FPM executes front/*.php → renders pages + calls plugin scripts  
     • PHP → may proxy AJAX/GraphQL calls to Python API (port configurable)  
   b. API layer (Python)  
     • Exposes endpoints: REST (api_server/*) and GraphQL  
     • Handles business logic: device scanning, heuristics, session/events  
     • Orchestrates workflows, scheduling, plugin invocation  
     • Persists & queries SQLite DB via server/database.py  
   c. Scheduler & workers  
     • Cron jobs (back/cron_script.sh or container crond) invoke scan scripts  
     • Python scheduler (server/scheduler.py) dispatches scan tasks & workflows  
     • Plugin scripts (front/plugins/**/script.py) implement scanners & notifications  
   d. Data layer  
     • SQLite database (db/app.db) for devices, events, config, workflows  
     • Versioned via SQL upgrade scripts (server/db/db_upgrade.py)  
   e. Plugin & notification framework  
     • Plugins live under front/plugins (scanner & notification handlers)  
     • Python server loads plugin metadata (server/plugin.py)  
     • Notifications via apprise or native Python modules (server/messaging)  
   f. Container orchestration  
     • Dockerfile builds a single image with Nginx, PHP, Python, Cron  
     • docker-compose.yml orchestrates service startup, volume mounts, networks  
     • .devcontainer for local VSCode development  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Separation of concerns:  
     • Presentation (PHP UI) vs Business (Python API) vs Data (SQLite)  
     • Plugin abstraction for scanners & gateways  
   - Layered architecture:  
     • Client ⇄ UI ⇄ API ⇄ DB  
     • Scheduler / Cron orthogonal to request flow  
   - Extensibility: all plugins follow a directory + config.json + script.py template  

5. Tailor the diagram for this full-stack, containerized app  
   - Group “services” running in the container:  
     [Nginx] → [PHP-FPM (front/)]  
     [Cron]  
     [Python API (server/)]  
   - Show volume mounts:  
     host/config ↔ /app/config  
     host/db ↔ /app/db  
     tmpfs ↔ /app/api  
   - Illustrate data flows:  
     • Browser → HTTP → Nginx → PHP-FPM → DB reads/writes  
     • PHP-FPM → HTTP → Python API → DB  
     • Cron → invokes Python or shell scripts → Python scheduler → DB  
     • Python API → triggers notifications → External services  
   - Highlight plugin paths:  
     • front/plugins/** → scanned by PHP UI for scheduling/config  
     • server/plugin_utils → loaded by Python API for scan execution  

6. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Components & shapes:  
     • Rectangle: service/process (Nginx, PHP-FPM, Python API, Cron)  
     • Cylinder: database (SQLite)  
     • Document icon: plugin script directory  
     • Cloud: external services (notification gateways, Home Assistant, webhooks)  
   - Arrows & labels:  
     • Directional arrows for request/response or data write/read  
     • Annotate protocols (HTTP, REST, GraphQL, shell invocation)  
   - Color coding:  
     • Green: presentation/UI layer  
     • Blue: backend/API layer  
     • Yellow: data layer  
     • Purple: plugin/extensibility  
     • Orange: external integrations  
   - Include:  
     • Clear component names (e.g., “PHP-FPM (front/)”)  
     • Port numbers (e.g., PORT=20211 for Python API)  
     • Volume mount paths  

7. Essential detail checklist  
   - Capture all four runtime services in the container  
   - Show scheduling vs request-driven flows separately  
   - Emphasize plugin directories & config.json files as extension points  
   - Depict the SQLite data store and upgrade path  
   - Represent external notification/integration services  

By following these steps, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate architecture diagram that reflects NetAlertX’s multi-service, plugin-friendly, containerized design.
